title: Sarcopenia narrative review: historical context, superseded for later trial results

Q01.answer: Review diabetes drugs as potential sarcopenia therapies. Narrative review; no registered systematic-review protocol reported. Biological rationale and research priorities. Not a randomized treatment study.

Q02.answer: Mixed cells, animals and human populations, many with type 2 diabetes. Heterogeneous settings and definitions of muscle health. No newly recruited or pooled participant population. Do not sum the review's study citations as independent trial participants.

Q03.answer: Multiple diabetes drug classes, including metformin. Different doses/routes across cited studies; no review-wide regimen. Exercise and other interventions vary. Durations differ by cited source. No universal schedule can be extracted from this review.

Q04.answer: Various placebo, usual-care and observational comparators. No new allocation. Randomization applies to individual cited trials only. No participant-level blinding in a narrative review. Literature available before publication in 2023. The review itself cannot remove bias from its sources.
locators: Evidence from observational and intervention studies

Q05.answer: No primary efficacy endpoint for the review. Muscle mass, strength, physical performance and proposed pathways. Varies by underlying study. Mix of clinical function and surrogates. No single meaningful-change threshold across this heterogeneous evidence. Muscle mass and physical function are distinct outcomes.

Q06.answer: Describes a positive small prefrailty study and blunted training adaptation in MASTERS. No pooled numerator or denominator. No meta-analytic estimate. Direction and context vary; no unified metformin benefit estimate. No review-level confidence interval or formal certainty analysis reported. For guide numbers, use the acquired primary reports rather than copying secondary summaries.

Q07.answer: No participant attrition in the review itself. No complete reproducible search or missing-study analysis. Adherence belongs to underlying trials. Systematic inclusion/exclusion and duplicate-screening process not reported. Narrative selected literature. Individual source study, with potential overlap. Unreported search methods limit confidence that all contradictory studies were included.

Q08.answer: Discusses gastrointestinal intolerance, lactic acidosis and class-specific risks. No review-wide exposure denominator. Qualitative safety discussion, not a new comparative safety estimate. No pooled treatment withdrawal count. Variable source durations. Current labels and directly assessed trials take precedence for guide safety facts.

Q09.answer: Narrative-selection and citation bias possible; heterogeneous designs. Observational diabetes-drug comparisons confounded by indication and health status. No prespecified systematic outcome hierarchy or formal bias assessment. No new inferential tests; selective emphasis across many studies remains possible. No pooled uncertainty estimate. Describes MET-PREVENT as underway; its 2025 results are now available. The forward-looking statement is historical, not a current missing trial.

Q10.answer: Research rationale for people with or at risk of sarcopenia. Does not identify a proven metformin regimen for those without diabetes. Does not establish benefit on falls, independence or survival. Diabetes observations cannot be transferred directly to frail adults without diabetes. Use as context only.

Q11.answer: Secondary review, no new study family. MASTERS is separately assessed; MET-PREVENT later reports results. Underlying trials must not be counted again through this review. Narrative scope, not an exhaustive updated search. Source count is not independent-study count.

Q12.answer: Miles Witham, Avan Sayer and colleagues. Geriatrics and muscle-research collaborators. No specific review funding; several authors acknowledge NIHR Newcastle Biomedical Research Centre support. No trial products supplied for this review. Witham and Sayer disclose being MET-PREVENT investigators. Retain that relevant disclosure without treating it as proof of bias.

Q13.answer: Published Drugs & Aging 2023, DOI 10.1007/s40266-023-01042-4. Full article acquired and relevant metformin sections assessed. No necessary separate meta-analysis dataset identified. No registered systematic-review protocol reported. No correction/retraction identified in retrieved records; time-sensitive trial-status statements superseded. November 3–4, 2026. This assessment is limited to its use as metformin background, not every drug class discussed.

Q14.answer: Why diabetes drugs were investigated for sarcopenia. Supports rationale and uncertainty, not demonstrated treatment efficacy. Authors call for trials; editorial synthesis includes later negative MET-PREVENT results. A historical review must not outrank a later directly relevant RCT.

Q15.answer: Mechanistic promise justified trials but was not proof of improved function. Optimal population and net effect remained unknown at publication. Later randomized functional outcomes should update the synthesis. MET-PREVENT now provides such evidence and is assessed separately.

appraisal: A useful narrative account of rationale and conflicting early evidence. It is neither a systematic efficacy synthesis nor an additional trial, and its description of MET-PREVENT as ongoing is superseded.
